page.layout: One page of running text in one column; the notes are in the left margin beside the main text, and at the foot of the text. Running head at the top, page number at the top right.

main_text.p: 7 O’ vtinam.) Primo verfu lego οὐ μ’ ἐτί, non ὃ μὴ τι. quod ☧ à metro est, ☧ à sensu alienū. Sed ad βάλε ἀλλ’ βάλε in margine est annotatum, κατ’ ἀποκοπὴν τῆς Α ἀρχῆς sοιχεῖα. ἐφι γὰρ τὸ ἐλον ἀβάλε sημαντικὸν sυχὴς ἐπίρρημα, αὐτὶ τῆς ὀφελον, εἴθε, ᾅθε. βάλε ait, praecifo α prima litera, pro ἀβάλε optandi aduerbio positum.
8 Tarandum.) Sic Aristotelēs θάωμας. ἀνὰς, non per τ, vt nostrum.
9 Cedripolis.) Vox vitiosa. Aristotelēs Amphipolim habet.

10 Veluti humidis & mollibus.) ὡς αὐ ἰνὺγωμ̄ ὄντων. Cur hederam gestarent, apud Aristotelem causa nō est explicata. Hoc quidem non celatum, aliquid doloris ob cornuum deiectionem esse ceruis. Vide num non sit legendū pro ἐμ, ἔτι: vt fortassis recens enata, ☧ adhuc tenera cornua edera munierint. Quod ad vocem Achainam attinet in margine (quantum quidem ego legere pos-sum) est Αχαϊνα ἱ☧ ἀαθίνα, ἰλίνιαι τινὲς ἐλάφων. Vide Apollonij Ἀργονωτ. ἀ. ☧ eius Scholiastam, paragr. 16. ☧ Eustath. Iliad. ϐ.
11 Aliquantulum.) ὀλίγον in Græco est, nō ὀλίγας. Cætera ex Aristotelis Mirabilibus narrationibus, ☧ Plutarchi libello de comparatione animalium terrestrium ☧ aquatilium, pete.
12 Prætereuntem enim.) Deest aliquid. Acsalonē diphthōgo scripsi, sicut ☧ Aristotelēs 9. de Hist.

page.notes: Greek and the ligature-like symbols (☧ stands for the printed &-like sign "&" in its curled form, which I could not confirm) are transcribed as best read. Several Greek words in the notes are doubtful, especially in notes 7, 10 and 12; they should be checked against the scan. The sign after "si" in note 12 and the last Greek forms in note 10 are uncertain. The catchword and signature are not visible at the foot. The final line of note 12 is set at the foot of the page and is partly cut off at the margin.
